claims.summary: Characteristic zero, every non-integer lambda (formal-lambda factorization, C(lambda) = const lambda^7 (lambda^2-1)^3 (lambda^2-4)). For four distinct nonzero roots b, the finite non-branch Weierstrass points of the degree-two pair space are the roots of the three polynomials numerator(b_i/(1+b_i t)+b_j/(1+b_j t)-b_k/(1+b_k t)-b_l/(1+b_l t)), one per matching, each of degree at most 2, with weights their multiplicities; the points are simple for generic roots.
claims.assessment: Working proof: translation identity phi_b(t+X)=(1+bt)^(-lambda) phi_(b/(1+bt))(X) and the exact factorization of the four-root Taylor determinant; exact equality of polynomials at three random configurations. Simplicity certified at (2,-3,5,7/2).
claims.rationale: Explicit Weierstrass points for four roots; the smallest separated case in closed form.

claims.summary: The pair-sum Vandermonde form of the pair-space Taylor determinant fails for M=5 (and every M>=5): with translation it would place every finite non-branch Weierstrass point of the cluster degeneration (eps b,1,-1) near 0 or +-1, contradicting the binary-face theorem (Q_3 has zeros +-i sqrt(3)/2); exactly, at roots (2,-3,5,7/2,-1/3) the predicted degree-30 product shares no factor with the Wronskian polynomial.
claims.assessment: Refutation by the binary-face theorem and an exact computation.

relationships: False for M>=5; true for M<=4.
